quandoUsar: A year of daily activity (commits, visits, workouts) where rhythm, streaks, and idle weeks matter more than the exact number for each day.
Switch years or ranges without redrawing: with new `days`, the grid recolors in a sweep and the total rolls digit by digit.
Let the user pick a day to filter what appears below, with `selectedDate` and `onSelectDate`.
quandoEvitar: Use `bar-chart` when exact comparison between days is the goal.
Use `returns-calendar` for daily values that can be negative, such as gains and losses; here, counts below zero become zero.
Use `date-picker` when the task is to choose a date, not to read activity.

teclado.acao: Enters the grid at the last day that had focus (or the selected one, or the most recent) and continues to the legend; only one day and one level are in the tab order.
Moves to the previous or next day.
In the grid, moves back or forward one week; in the legend, moves to the previous or next level.
Moves to the first or last day of the range; in the legend, to the first or last level.
In the grid, selects the focused day and calls `onSelectDate`; in the legend, pins or unpins the level highlight.
Closes the tooltip of the focused day; in the legend, cancels the level preview.

acessibilidade: The grid has `role="grid"` with its name coming from `label` (required), and each day is a `gridcell` whose `aria-label` carries the count and the full date.
The total sits in a hidden `role="status"` region; the legend levels are buttons with `aria-pressed`, and an `aria-live` text says how many days are in the highlighted level.
The fixed texts (“No …”, “in”, “Less”, “More”, “days with”) are in English in the code: `locale` only changes dates and numbers, and `unit` only the nouns of the count.
movimento: The first time it enters the screen, the squares appear in a diagonal wave of about 0.4 s; a new range recolors the grid along the same diagonal, forward or backward depending on the date.
A single tooltip slides with a spring from one day to another, and the selection ring slides to the chosen day.
With “reduce motion”, the grid appears all at once, the tooltip jumps into place, and swaps become a short fade.
responsivo: The square size goes from 9 to 15 px depending on the container width; below about 670 px the grid scrolls sideways, starts at the most recent weeks, and keeps the weekday labels fixed on the left.
In containers up to 440 px the legend shortens to just the day count; if the background is not `--surface`, set `--heatmap-surface` so the fixed labels cover the scrolling grid.
desempenho: There are about 370 memoized cells, with events delegated to the grid; pass `days`, `thresholds`, and `onSelectDate` with a stable reference (`useMemo`, `useCallback`) so all of them are not redone on every render.
notasIA: `days` is a list of `{ date: "YYYY-MM-DD", count }` from the oldest day to the newest, read in UTC; missing days count as zero, and `label` and `period` are required.
Selection is controlled only: keep `selectedDate` in the parent and update it in `onSelectDate`; without that callback, clicking a day does nothing.
Put the year selector in `actions` (a `segmented-control`, for example) and change only `days`: changing the component's `key` remounts the grid and loses the recoloring sweep.

quandoUsar: Dashboard totals that change with the period or filter: each digit spins like an odometer in the direction the number moved.
Highlight numbers that count up from zero when they enter the screen, with `animateOnView`.
Values with currency, percentage, or decimal places, via `prefix`, `suffix`, and `decimals`.
quandoEvitar: Use `metric-card` when the number needs a label, context, and change in a ready-made card.
Use `slot-text` when the value mixes letters and numbers or the swap should look like a slot machine.
Use `countdown` for a countdown to a date.
acessibilidade: The animated digits are `aria-hidden`; the screen reader receives a hidden text with the already formatted number, including `prefix` and `suffix`.
There is no live region: if the value change needs to be announced, wrap the counter in an element with `aria-live`.
The visible digits have `user-select: none`, so the number cannot be selected for copying.
movimento: Each digit is a 0 to 9 wheel that spins with a no-overshoot spring in the direction of the change (upward when the value grows), going from 9 to 0 like an odometer.
When the number gains or loses places, the columns open or close in width; with `animateOnView`, the digits rise from zero in a cascade when 60% of the counter is visible.
With “reduce motion”, the digits change immediately and the label only fades.
desempenho: Each digit mounts ten animated glyphs (a seven-digit number is 70 elements), so use it on a few highlights per screen, not on every row of a table.
notasIA: `value` must be a `number`; formatting uses `locale` (default `en-US`, fixed so server and client render the same), so pass `locale="pt-BR"` for a dot thousands separator and a decimal comma.

It accepts neither `className` nor `style`, and the size comes from `--text-3xl` on the component itself: a `font-size` on the parent element changes nothing; redefine that variable on a surrounding element.
Just change `value` to animate; do not change the component's `key`, otherwise it remounts already at the new value, without spinning.

quandoUsar: A preview that switches between landscape, square, and portrait (a crop format selector, for example) without layout shift.
Reserve the space of an image, video, or `iframe` before loading, with the media cropped from the center.
Vertical formats that should not push the page: with `maxHeight` the box narrows instead of growing.
quandoEvitar: When the ratio never changes and there is no cropping, the CSS `aspect-ratio` property does the job without a client component.
Use `image-compare` to compare two images with a divider.
Use `image-viewer` when photos need to open enlarged, with zoom and navigation.
acessibilidade: It is a `div` with no role or label: the description comes from the media you place inside, so provide `alt` on the image or `title` on the `iframe`.
movimento: When `ratio` changes, the ratio itself animates with a no-overshoot spring and the browser recalculates width and height on every frame, so the media never stretches as it would with a `scale`.
The first render does not animate; `animated={false}` swaps immediately, and with “reduce motion” the swap is always instant.
responsivo: The box takes 100% of the parent's width; with `maxHeight` the width becomes the smaller of 100% and `maxHeight` times the ratio, and the box is centered in the row.
desempenho: The animation touches layout, not `transform`: each frame recalculates the box and what comes after it, which is light for a preview and heavy for a whole grid changing ratio at the same time.
notasIA: `ratio` accepts a number (`16 / 9`) or text (`"16/9"`, `"16:9"`, `"1.85"`); an unreadable value falls back to 16:9 without a warning.

Direct children `img`, `video`, `canvas`, `iframe`, and `picture` are stretched over the box and cropped (`fit="contain"` shows the whole media); other children you position yourself, since the box is `position: relative`.
`onRatioSettled` fires when the box settles on a new ratio (it does not fire on mount); the parent must define the width.

quandoUsar: Identify a person or account next to the name, in a comment, a list row, or the header.
Show presence with `status` (`online` or `offline`), as a dot at the corner of the avatar.
Lists where not everyone has a photo: without `src`, or if the image fails, the initials of `name` appear.
quandoEvitar: Use `avatar-group` for several people stacked in a small space.
Use `user-menu` when the avatar opens the account menu.
For logos and images that do not represent someone, use a regular image: the crop is always circular and the fallback to the photo is a name's initials.
acessibilidade: The `span` gets `role="img"` and `aria-label` with `name` and, if present, the status; the photo has an empty `alt` and the initials are `aria-hidden`.
`role` and `aria-label` passed through props are overwritten; when the name already appears as text next to it, pass `aria-hidden` so the screen reader does not repeat it.
The status goes into the label in English (“online”, “offline”) and, on screen, is just a colored dot.
movimento: A photo still loading emerges from a slight blur; one already cached appears immediately, and the fallback initials enter with a fade.
The status dot appears and swaps with a small spring scale; with “reduce motion”, photo, initials, and dot change without transition.
responsivo: Sizes are fixed in pixels (`sm` 28, `md` 36, `lg` 48, `xl` 88) and the avatar does not shrink inside a flex row.
desempenho: The photo goes through the image component from `RyanProvider`: by default an `` with `loading="lazy"`; with `next/image` it receives `fill` and the `sizes` of the chosen size.
notasIA: `name` is required even with a photo: the accessible label and the initials (first letter of the first two words) come from it.
It is not interactive and does not receive focus: for a clickable avatar, wrap it in a `button` or link with its own name, or use `user-menu`.
The export is named, with no default: `import { Avatar } from "@/components/ryan-ui/avatar/avatar"`; extra props go to the root `span`.

quandoUsar: Show who takes part in a project, document, or team in little space: header, card, or table cell.
Lists that change live: whoever joins or leaves opens or closes their own space and the rest of the stack slides.
Groups larger than the space: `max` limits the visible avatars and the remainder becomes a `+N` counter.
quandoEvitar: Use `avatar` for a single person.
When each person needs to be clickable or the full list must be in view, use a list with names: here nothing receives focus and anyone beyond `max` is not shown.
acessibilidade: The container is a `role="group"` named by `label` (the default is English, “Team members”); each avatar announces the name, and the counter announces “N more” followed by the label.
The name bubble is visual only: it appears on mouse hover and is `aria-hidden`; on touch it does not appear, and the names beyond `max` are not available anywhere.
movimento: A new member opens its own width with a no-overshoot spring and the others slide; whoever leaves closes the space the same way.
The `+N` counter rolls in the direction of the change: the new number rises when there are more people and drops when there are fewer.
With “reduce motion”, entries, exits, and the counter swap immediately and the name bubble appears without rising.
notasIA: `members` is a list of `{ name, src?, status? }` and `name` serves as the `key`: two members with the same name cause a React warning and break the animation.
To see animated entry and exit, change the `members` list while the component is mounted; `max` (default 4) decides how many appear before the `+N`.
It depends on `avatar` and only accepts `size` `sm`, `md`, or `lg`; pass `label` in your language, because the default is English.

quandoUsar: The state of a record in a table, list, or card (Active, Overdue, Failed), with `tone` and, if you like, the `dot` indicator.
Categories with no state meaning, such as HTTP methods or labels, with the six `color` options.
A label that changes in place (Draft → Published): the text swaps and the width follows with a spring.
quandoEvitar: Use `tag-input` for values the user types and removes.
Use `chip-group` for filters that toggle on and off: the badge is not clickable and does not receive focus.
Use `alert` when the message needs an explanation or an action.
acessibilidade: It is a `span` with no role: the screen reader reads only the text, so the word itself must state the status; the `tone` color and the dot are not announced.
Icon and dot are `aria-hidden`, and during the swap so is the outgoing copy, so the text is not read twice.
A text change is not announced on its own; if needed, pass `role="status"` (extra props go to the `span`).
movimento: When the text changes, the old one rises and disappears, the new one enters from below with a slight blur, and the width goes from the old size to the new with a no-overshoot spring.
An icon from another component swaps with scale and fade; changing `tone` or `color` makes background, border, and text change color in a short transition.
With “reduce motion”, text and icon only fade quickly and the width follows immediately.
responsivo: The badge does not wrap or shrink (`white-space: nowrap`, `flex: none`): in narrow columns use short labels or `size="sm"`.
desempenho: Each badge keeps a size observer for the width animation; in a table with hundreds of rows this adds up, so paginate or virtualize.
notasIA: Use `tone` for status (`neutral`, `success`, `info`, `warning`, `danger`) and `color` for category; `color` wins over `tone`, and `dot` is ignored when there is an `icon`.
Pass the label as plain text (`<Badge>{status}</Badge>`): the animated swap only happens when the child is a string or number, not JSX.
The `icon` SVG is resized by CSS to 12, 14, or 16 px depending on `size`; `outline` and `pill` only change the border and corners.

quandoUsar: A measure over days, weeks, or months, when the user compares each period with the others and with the average.
Switch ranges (week, 30 days) without redrawing: bars with the same `key` stay in place and the axis zooms in or out around the most recent one.
Touch reading: dragging a finger over the bars shows each one's value in the title.
quandoEvitar: Use `line-chart` for more than one series or when the shape of the trend matters more than each value.
Use `sparkline` for a compact trend next to a number, without axes.
Use `composition-chart` for the parts of a whole; this chart shows a single measure and does not draw negative values.

teclado.acao: Moves focus to the chart area, which behaves as a `slider`, and activates the most recent bar.
Moves to the previous bar.
Moves to the next bar.
Moves forward or back seven bars.
Moves to the first or last bar.
Leaves reading mode: the title shows the average again.

acessibilidade: The reading area is a focusable `role="slider"` whose `aria-valuetext` states the label and value of the active bar; the SVG is an `img` with a summary of the average, highest, and lowest value.
A hidden table lists every point for the screen reader, and an `aria-live` region announces the period and average when the data changes.
`label` and `period` are required and name the chart; “Avg”, “Highest”, and “Lowest” are in English in the code, but `averageLabel`, `valueLabel`, and `categoryLabel` are yours.
movimento: The bars grow from the base, left to right, when the chart enters the screen, and the average line rises with them.
On a new range, the time axis zooms in or out with a spring around the most recent bar: the bars that stay change height in place, those that leave sink to the base, and the average slides.
With “reduce motion”, heights, scale, and cursor jump to the final value and the title texts only fade.
responsivo: The chart measures its own width, and the axis labels thin out (every other one, and so on, counting from the most recent bar) so they do not touch.
The reading layer uses `touch-action: pan-y`: dragging horizontally reads the bars and vertically keeps scrolling the page; the height is fixed at `height` (176 px by default).
desempenho: Each bar is a `path` recalculated on every frame during transitions and takes 58% of its slice (at most 28 px): the component serves dozens of bars, not hundreds.
notasIA: Each point is `{ key, label, axisLabel?, value }`, from oldest to newest; the `key` must be stable (an ISO date) so the range swap transforms the bars instead of redrawing.
The active bar is internal state: there is no prop or callback to read or control which one is being read.
The title average is rounded to an integer before `formatValue`, and the default format has no decimal places: for fractional measures, pass the values in a smaller unit.

quandoUsar: A long, dense time series where the user needs the whole history and a close look at any stretch.
Mark events in the series (launches, price changes) with `annotations` and read each one on the chart itself.
Sync the window with shortcuts or other panels, through `range` and `onRangeChange`.
quandoEvitar: Use `line-chart` to compare more than one series: here there is only one.
Use `bar-chart` for a few periods compared one by one and against the average.
Use `sparkline` for a compact trend next to a number.

teclado.acao: Goes through four stops: the chart, the overview strip window, the start handle, and the end handle.
On the chart, move the reading to the previous point, the next, the first, and the last visible point.
On the window, shift the range by 10% of its width; on a handle, move that edge one point; with `Shift`, the step becomes 50% or ten points.
On the chart, jump about one eighth of the visible points; on the window and handles, take the large step.
With focus on the window, zoom in (half the range) or out (double).
On the window or handles, return to the whole series; on the chart, `Esc` clears the reading.

acessibilidade: The chart is a focusable group that announces the date and value of the point being read in an `aria-live` region; a hidden table carries the points and events of the current window.
The window and the two handles are `role="slider"` with `aria-valuetext` in dates, and each one is a `Tab` stop.
`label` is required; the group instruction, the handle names, and the axis dates are in English in the code (`formatDate` only changes the tooltip and announcements).
movimento: The line draws from left to right the first time it appears; on zoom in, the value axis adjusts with a spring to the highest point in the window.

The window follows the finger with no delay while dragging and slides with a spring when `range` changes externally or when it returns to the whole series; the tooltip follows the crosshair with a spring.
With “reduce motion”, the line already appears whole, the window and axis jump to the destination, and the tooltip follows without a spring.
responsivo: It measures its own width: date labels move from days to weeks, months, quarters, and years depending on space, and event labels that would collide are hidden.
Chart and strip use `touch-action: pan-y`, so dragging vertically keeps scrolling the page; heights come from `height` (240) and `overviewHeight` (52), in pixels.
desempenho: Above two points per pixel the line keeps only the minimum and maximum of each column; the hidden table, however, has one row per point in the window, so aggregate very long series before passing them.
Keep `data` and `annotations` with a stable reference (`useMemo`): smoothing and the overview strip are recalculated whenever they change.
notasIA: `data` is `{ date, value }` with `date` as a `Date` or milliseconds, in ascending order; with fewer than two points `emptyLabel` appears, and the value axis always starts at zero.

`range` is a target, not a lock: the window moves on its own while dragging and only slides when `range` changes, so keep what comes from `onRangeChange` in state; without `range`, use `defaultRange`.
The component assumes one point per day: when zoomed out the line becomes a seven-point average with a band, and the tooltip compares with seven points earlier, calling it “a week earlier”.

quandoUsar: When order matters more than values: who led, who overtook whom, and in which period.
Rankings by period with few items, such as regions by month or teams by round, with each series' name at the end of its line.
Switch the ranking measure while keeping the items: series with the same `key` slide to the new positions.
quandoEvitar: Use `line-chart` when the distance between values matters: here only the position appears in the drawing.
Use `slope-chart` to compare exactly two moments.
Use `sortable-data-table` for the ranking of a single period with several columns.

teclado.acao: Moves focus to the chart area and brings forward the series that is first in the last period.
Moves to the series one position above or below in the current period.
Moves to the previous or next period, keeping the series.
Moves to the first or last period.
Releases the series: all return to the same weight.

acessibilidade: The reading area is a vertical `role="slider"` whose `aria-valuetext` states the series, period, position, value, and the change since the previous period.
A hidden table carries the position and value of each series in each period; `label` is required and names the figure.
Ordinals and tooltip phrases (“1st of 6”, “Up 2 from Oct”) are generated in English in the code and have no translation prop.
movimento: On first appearance each line draws from the first to the last period, one series after another, and the points appear following the stroke.

When the data changes, lines, points, and names slide with a no-overshoot spring to the new positions; the focused series gets a thicker stroke and a ring with the position in each period, and the others fade.
With “reduce motion”, everything appears and swaps immediately, and the tooltip jumps instead of sliding.
responsivo: The height is `rowHeight` (40 px) times the number of series and the width is the container's; the names column takes up to 36% and truncates with an ellipsis.
Period labels do not thin out when space runs short: with many periods on a narrow screen they overlap, so use short labels.
notasIA: Each series is `{ key, label, values, color? }`, with one value per item in `periods` in the same order; positions are computed from the values, and `order="asc"` puts the smallest first (times, costs).
Focused series: controlled with `activeKey` and `onActiveChange` (`null` for none), or uncontrolled with `defaultActiveKey`.
The first four series use `--series-1` to `--series-4` and the following ones, three neutral tones that repeat from the eighth: pass `color` if there are more.

quandoUsar: Open, high, low, and close prices over a sequence of trading sessions or periods.
Exact reading of a period: the crosshair snaps to each candle and the tooltip shows the four prices, the change, and the volume.
Switch ranges (1 month, 3 months): candles with the same `key` slide to the new place.
quandoEvitar: Use `line-chart` when the close is enough or assets need to be compared.
Use `brush-chart` for long histories that need zoom: here all the candles in `data` stay on screen.
Use `sparkline` for a compact trend next to a price.

teclado.acao: Moves focus to the chart area and activates the most recent candle.
Moves to the previous candle.
Moves to the next candle.
Moves forward or back five candles.
Moves to the first or last candle.
Removes the crosshair and closes the tooltip.

acessibilidade: The reading area is a `role="slider"` whose `aria-valuetext` carries the period label and the four prices; a hidden table lists all the candles.
Up and down are distinguished by color only (`--success` and `--danger`); the sign of the change appears in the tooltip, not in the drawing.
`label` is required; “Open”, “High”, “Low”, “Close”, and “Volume” are in English in the code.
movimento: On first appearance the candles grow from a line at body height, left to right; the last close line appears next.
The vertical crosshair snaps to the candle and slides with a spring between them, with the tooltip alongside; the horizontal line follows the pointer or, by keyboard, rests on the close.
With “reduce motion”, candles, grid, and crosshair appear and change without transition.
responsivo: The width is the container's: each candle's body takes 62% of its slice, between 1.5 and 14 px, and the axis labels keep at least 58 px between them.
The tooltip moves to the left of the candle when it does not fit on the right, and the reading layer uses `touch-action: pan-y` so the page keeps scrolling vertically.
desempenho: Each candle is an animated `path` and the body never goes below 1.5 px: with more candles than the width can hold they overlap, so aggregate into larger periods.
notasIA: Each candle is `{ key, label, axisLabel?, open, high, low, close, volume? }`, from oldest to newest; set `axisLabel` on only some (every Monday, for example).
The crosshair can be controlled with `activeIndex` and `onActiveChange`, useful for syncing with another chart; otherwise, use `defaultActiveIndex` or leave it free.
`formatValue` formats the axis, title, and tooltip (the default has two decimal places and no currency symbol); the title's change is the last close minus the first open in `data`.

quandoUsar: Group a title, short description, media, and one or two actions about the same object (a project, an itinerary, an article) in a grid or list.
A summary that opens a larger quick look without leaving the page: with `details`, the whole card becomes the trigger and grows into a central panel.
A footer with the owner and a state that changes in place, such as “Updated just now”, announced to the screen reader.
quandoEvitar: Use `expandable-card` when the extra content should open in place, within the page flow, and not in a dialog.
Use `metric-card` for a number with context and change.
Use `dialog` for decisions and forms that do not start from a card: the quick look here is for reading more about the same item.

teclado.acao: With `details`, stops on the title, which becomes a button; focus appears as a stronger card border.
Open the quick look from the title.
Closes the quick look: the panel returns to the card's place and focus returns to the title.
With the quick look open, cycle only among the panel's controls.

acessibilidade: The card is an `article` with an `h3` title; the quick look is a Radix modal dialog (traps focus, closes with `Esc` or outside click, and returns focus) with the title as `h2` and the description linked by `aria-describedby`.
With `details`, the title's click area covers the whole card and `action` sits on top; the title button has no outline of its own, only the card border changes on focus.
`status` is a `role="status"` region, so each new text is announced; the close button has an English label (“Close quick look”), and the media `alt` is up to you.
movimento: Under the mouse pointer the card rises 2 px with a shadow and the media slowly zooms in to 4%.

In the quick look, the surface, photo, title, description, and footer travel on a no-overshoot spring from the card to the central panel and return along the same path on closing; `details` enters after the panel has grown.
With “reduce motion”, the card neither rises nor zooms the photo, the quick look only fades, and `status` swaps without animation.
responsivo: The quick look panel is `min(100vw - var(--space-8), 30rem)` wide and at most the screen height minus the same margin, with internal scrolling.
The card takes the parent's width; in a narrow footer, `meta` and `status` truncate with an ellipsis instead of going under `action`.
desempenho: Each card with `details` mounts its own dialog and a size observer, and the quick look backdrop uses `backdrop-filter`; in long grids, pass `details` only where it is needed.
notasIA: `title` is required and is text; `media`, `avatar`, `meta`, `action`, `children`, and `details` are free slots, and `status` must be a string because it animates word by word.
`open`, `defaultOpen`, and `onOpenChange` only apply with `details`; without it the card is static and the title does not become a button.
With the quick look open, `media`, `children`, `avatar`, and `action` exist twice (in the card and in the panel): do not put a fixed `id` or local state inside them.

quandoUsar: Quick triage, one item at a time, where each deserves a moment of attention: selecting destinations, candidates, or design options.
Two-sided decisions (keep or pass) with undo, by dragging, with the buttons, or with the keyboard arrow keys.
Long decks: only four cards are mounted at a time.
quandoEvitar: Use `sortable-data-table` when people need to compare items side by side.
Use `carousel` to browse a set without deciding anything about each item.
Use `swipe-actions` for swipe actions on the rows of a list; here there are only two outcomes per card.

teclado.acao: Moves focus to the stack (the outline appears on the top card) and then to the three buttons.
With focus on the stack, decide the top card to the left or to the right.
With focus on the stack, undo the last decision and bring the card back.
Trigger the focused button: reject, undo, or accept.

acessibilidade: The stack is a focusable group with `aria-roledescription="card stack"` and a hidden hint with the keys; the top card announces its name and position (via `getLabel`) and the ones behind are `inert`.
Each decision, undo, and restart is announced in a `role="status"` region; `outcomes` supplies the verb of the sentence, but the rest of it (“3 left.”, “restored”) is fixed English.
The buttons use `aria-disabled` to keep focus when the stack runs out; the key hint, “Undo”, and the default empty state are also in English (`renderEmpty` replaces the empty state).
movimento: The top card follows the finger, rotates with the displacement, and shows the stamp of the chosen side; the ones behind rise gradually as it moves away.
Released beyond 35% of the width (at most 140 px) or on a fast swipe, it flies off with a spring in the direction of the gesture; before that, it returns to its place with a spring.
Undo brings the card back from where it left; with “reduce motion”, leaving and returning are just a fade and the ones behind swap places immediately.
responsivo: The stack is up to 20rem wide with a fixed height of 19rem (17.5rem on screens up to 26rem); the content of `renderCard` should fill 100% of the height.
On screens up to 22.5rem the undo button keeps only the icon, retaining its accessible name; the card uses `touch-action: pan-y`, so dragging vertically scrolls the page.
desempenho: Only the next four cards (and those still flying off) stay in the DOM, so the size of `items` does not weigh on rendering.
notasIA: `items`, `getKey`, `getLabel`, and `renderCard` are required; position is internal state and the parent receives `onDecide(item, "left" | "right")`, `onUndo`, and `onReset`.
Keep `items` stable: position is stored by index, so removing the decided item from the list inside `onDecide` makes the next card get skipped.
Handle `onUndo` and `onReset` along with `onDecide`, otherwise your list of chosen items diverges from the stack; `labels` names the buttons and the stamps.

quandoUsar: A short, ordered set of items of the same kind, such as products or case studies, where the neighbors in view signal that there is more.
Touch navigation (drag, quick swipe, horizontal trackpad gesture) with equivalent arrows, indicators, and keyboard.
Optional automatic rotation with a visible pause button, via `interval`.
quandoEvitar: Use `marquee` for a strip that scrolls on its own without stopping at each item, such as a row of logos.
Use `image-viewer` for photos that need to open enlarged, with zoom.
Use `card-stack` when the user decides on each item instead of just browsing.

teclado.acao: Go to the previous or next slide, with focus anywhere in the carousel outside text fields.
Go to the first or last slide.
Moves through the slides area, the active slide's content, the rotation button, the selected indicator, and the two arrows.
Trigger the focused button: pause or start rotation, choose a slide, previous or next.

acessibilidade: The `section` has `aria-roledescription="carousel"` and the name from `label`; each slide is a `tabpanel` labeled by `slideLabel`, and the indicators form a `tablist` in which only the selected one is in the tab order.
Slides away from the center are `inert`: links and buttons inside them only work on the active slide, and a manual change is announced in an `aria-live` region.
Rotation pauses on mouse hover, on keyboard focus, while dragging, off screen, and with the tab hidden; the control labels (“Next slide”, “Pause slide rotation”) are in English in the code.
movimento: The track goes to the slide with a no-overshoot spring, carrying the gesture's velocity; at the ends it resists like an elastic band.

Slides shrink to 90% and fade to 50% as they move away from the center, and the indicator stretches into a pill that travels along with it, frame by frame; during rotation, the pill empties until the swap.
With “reduce motion”, the track jumps to the slide and automatic rotation is unavailable (the button does not even appear).
responsivo: The root is a size container and needs a defined width; `slideSize` (default `min(80cqw, 340px)`) accepts any CSS length, and `cqw` is the fraction of the carousel's width.
With a container up to 340 px the controls row tightens; the slides area uses `touch-action: pan-y`, so the vertical gesture scrolls the page.
desempenho: All slides stay mounted and read the track position on every frame for scale and opacity: keep the set short.
With `interval`, an `IntersectionObserver` and the page visibility event pause rotation when no one is looking.
notasIA: Each child is a slide (give it a stable `key`) and `label` is required; index controlled with `index` and `onIndexChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultIndex`.
`interval` (ms per slide) only adds the rotation button; it starts stopped, unless you pass `autoplay`.
There is no loop: the arrows stop at the first and last slide, and only automatic rotation returns to the start.

quandoUsar: Conversation between people or customer support: messages grouped by author and by day, reactions, typing indicator, and read receipts.
When the delivery state of the user's own message matters: sending, sent, delivered, read, or failed, with a retry button via `onRetry`.
When the user attaches files with the button, by pasting, or by dragging onto the composer.
quandoEvitar: Use `chat-app` for a conversation with an AI assistant, with streaming responses, stop, and regenerate.
Use `comment-thread` for a discussion tied to a piece of content, with nested replies, mentions, editing, and resolve.
Use `message-bubble` when you only need the bubble, without a list, scrolling, or composer.

teclado.acao: In the message field, sends the text and attachments.
Inserts a line break without sending.
In the reaction picker, move from one emoji to another, wrapping at the ends.
Closes the reaction picker and returns focus to the button that opened it.
On a reaction under the message, toggle your participation; in the picker, choose the focused emoji.
Moves through attachments, reactions, the new messages pill, attach, field, and send; a message's react button appears when focus enters it.

acessibilidade: The list is a `role="log"` with `aria-live="polite"`, so new messages are announced; who is typing is announced in a separate `role="status"` region.
Reactions are buttons with `aria-pressed` and a label with the count; the picker opens with focus on the first emoji and returns it on closing.
All visible or announced text has an English default and can be replaced through `labels`; also provide `label` (the conversation's name) and `alt` on image attachments.
movimento: Each new message pops in from its side with a spring and, if you are at the end, the conversation rises from where it was instead of jumping.
Reactions appear with scale and the count rolls; the read avatars slide to the last read message, and the typing dots pulse in sequence.
With “reduce motion”, everything becomes a short fade, the dots stay still, and scrolling to the end is instant.
responsivo: The root has `height: 100%` and scrolls internally: the parent must have a defined height, otherwise the list neither scrolls nor stays pinned to the end.
Bubbles take up to 78% of the width (84% on screens up to 420 px), and on touch screens the react button is always visible.
desempenho: All messages stay in the DOM, without virtualization: for long histories, load in pages.
Images use `loading="lazy"`, and `width` and `height` on the attachment reserve the space of a single image before it loads.
notasIA: With `messages` (controlled) you add the message yourself in `onSend` and update reactions in `onReact`; with `defaultMessages` the list handles this and the callbacks only notify.
`onSend` receives `{ text, files }` with `File` objects that you must upload to the server; `currentUserId` sets the side of the bubbles, and each `authorId` must exist in `participants`.
Message text is plain, without markdown; `ChatComposer` is exported separately, and the `ref` offers `scrollToBottom()` and `focusComposer()`.

quandoUsar: Show a code snippet in documentation or a tutorial, with file name, language, and a copy button.
Long sources that should start collapsed: `maxLines` cuts the height and a button opens the rest in place.
Code that changes in the same block (variations by package manager or framework): the new code enters smoothly and the height follows.
quandoEvitar: Use `file-diff` to show what changed between two versions of a file.
Use `json-viewer` to explore JSON data with nodes that open and close and with search.
Use `copy-button` alone to copy a short value, such as a token or a one-line command.

teclado.acao: Moves through the copy button, the code block (which is focusable), and, if present, the expand button.
Trigger the focused button: copy, or show all lines and collapse.
With focus on the code, scroll long lines sideways; this is the native scrolling of the `pre`, which receives `tabIndex` for that.

acessibilidade: The block is a `section` labeled with the file name or the language; the `pre` is focusable for scrolling by keyboard, and the expand button reports `aria-expanded`.
When collapsed, the code is only clipped in height: the screen reader and the copy button still have the full text.
Copying is confirmed in a `role="status"` region of the `copy-button`; the labels (“Copy code”, “Show all N lines”) are in English in the code.
movimento: Expanding and collapsing animates the height with a no-overshoot spring, rotates the arrow, and swaps the button label.
A new `code` enters rising 4 px while the height follows the content, and a new `filename` swaps with the width following on a spring.
With “reduce motion”, height, texts, and arrow change immediately.
responsivo: Long lines do not wrap: they scroll sideways inside the block, which takes 100% of the parent's width.
On screens up to 420 px the font and spacing shrink and the copy button keeps only the icon.
desempenho: Highlighting runs on every render over the whole code and creates one `span` per token, even when collapsed: for files with thousands of lines, show an excerpt.
notasIA: `language` (default `tsx`) defines the label and the highlighting heuristics, a simple tokenizer aimed at JS/TS, JSON, HTML, and CSS; in `bash` or `python`, comments with `#` are not recognized.
Pass `code` without a trailing line break: it counts as one extra line in the “Show all N lines” button.
It depends on `copy-button`, the export is named (`CodeBlock`), and the expanded state is internal; there is no `className`, line numbers, or line highlighting.

quandoUsar: A discussion tied to specific content (a layout heading, a paragraph, a task), with the subject in `title`.
When the conversation needs nested replies, reactions, `@` mentions, and editing or deleting your own comments in place.
Reviews that wrap up: resolving folds the whole conversation into a one-line summary that can be reopened.
quandoEvitar: Use `chat-thread` for real-time conversation, with bubbles, typing indicator, and read receipts.
Use `mention-input` when you only need the field with mentions, without the surrounding conversation.
Use `timeline` for a read-only history of what happened.

teclado.acao: Submit the comment or save the edit; `Enter` alone inserts a line break.
With the mention suggestions open, move through the list.
With the suggestions open, insert the highlighted person as `@Nome Completo`.
Closes the suggestions; without them, cancels the reply or edit, and also closes the reaction picker and the delete confirmation.
Moves through each comment's buttons; the actions (react, reply, edit, delete) appear when focus enters it.

acessibilidade: The root is a named `section` and each comment is an `article` with author and time in the label; the field is a `combobox` linked to the mentions list by `aria-activedescendant`.
Focus is guided: resolving moves to the reopen button and vice versa, replying moves to the field, and the delete confirmation opens with focus on the delete button.
All texts have an English default and are replaced through `labels`; there is no live region, so comments arriving from elsewhere are not announced.
movimento: Comments and replies enter and leave by opening their own height with a spring; collapsing replies does the same and rotates the arrow.
Editing swaps the text for the field with a fade while the comment's height follows on a spring; reactions appear with scale and the count rolls.
Resolving crossfades the conversation with the summary while the box height animates; with “reduce motion”, short fades remain and heights change immediately.
responsivo: On screens up to 420 px the field loses the avatar beside it and replies indent 12 px instead of 24; on touch, each comment's actions are always visible.
The field grows with the text through `field-sizing: content` (up to 160 px); in browsers without that property it stays at one line and scrolls.
desempenho: The whole tree is rebuilt on every change and each comment keeps a height observer: it serves discussions of dozens of comments, not a long feed.
notasIA: Controlled or not on both axes: `comments` with `onCommentsChange` and `resolved` with `onResolvedChange`, or `defaultComments` and `defaultResolved`; the callback delivers the whole new tree and the event that caused it, to sync the server.
`createdAt` is the already formatted text (“2h”, “Sep 18”), not a date; new comments go out with `nowLabel` and a local `id`, which you swap for the server's.
`currentUser` decides who can edit and delete; `people` feeds the mentions, and replies beyond `maxDepth` (2) attach to the deepest allowed level.

quandoUsar: The parts of a single whole when each one's share matters more than the history: spend by service, revenue by plan.
Let the user take a part out of the calculation: each legend row turns the part off or on and the others redistribute in the bar.
Compare the same parts across periods: with the same `key`s, the segments slide to the new shares.
quandoEvitar: Use `usage-meter` when the parts fill a fixed limit, such as a plan's storage.
Use `treemap` for parts within parts, with navigation by levels.
Use `streamgraph` when how the mix changes over time is what matters.

teclado.acao: Moves through the legend rows; the focused part stands out in the bar and shows the tooltip.
Turn the focused part off or on; the last visible part cannot be turned off.

acessibilidade: The bar is `aria-hidden`: the data comes from the legend, where each row is a button with `aria-pressed`, name, value, and share.
The title total is also `aria-hidden`: if it is essential, repeat it in `label`, which is required and names the figure.
“Value”, “Share”, “Hidden”, and the legend instruction are in English in the code; only `label`, `totalLabel`, and the part names are yours.
movimento: On first appearance the segments grow from the left edge, one after another, and the total and percentages count up from zero.
With new data or a part turned off, the segments slide with a no-overshoot spring to the new widths; the one turned off folds away until it disappears where it was.
The focused segment grows 3 px up and down and the tooltip slides to it; with “reduce motion”, widths and numbers change immediately.
responsivo: The bar measures the container's width, and the legend is a grid with columns of at least 232 px, which becomes a single column when space runs short.
notasIA: Each part is `{ key, label, value, color? }` in the order it should appear; parts with a zero value stay out of the bar and appear in the legend as “Hidden”, so filter beforehand.
Total and percentages are computed over the visible parts: turning one off decreases the title total; control with `hiddenKeys` and `onHiddenChange`, or use `defaultHiddenKeys`.
The first four parts use `--series-1` to `--series-4` and the following ones, three neutral tones that repeat from the eighth: group the rest into “Other” or pass `color`.
